atlas_home_region_card.compact: A California-coded early guitar-pop lane split between reverb-soaked instrumentals and harmony-rich beach-radio songs.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It made guitar tone an environment. Its reverb, tremolo, fast picking, and wordless hooks echo through garage rock, film music, punk revival, and guitar instrumental culture.

region_scene_page.compact: Surf music turns place into sound: ocean motion, hot rods, Southern California youth imagery, and electric-guitar technology.
region_scene_page.standard: Surf music turns place into sound: ocean motion, hot rods, Southern California youth imagery, and electric-guitar technology. Duane Eddy's Rebel-'Rouser, The Ventures' Perfidia, Annette Funicello's Pineapple Princess, and Dick Dale and His Del-Tones' Misirlou give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Surf music turns place into sound: ocean motion, hot rods, Southern California youth imagery, and electric-guitar technology. The record often feels horizontal and kinetic, like motion across a surface: rolling drums, wet guitar, bright harmonies, and a scene you can picture immediately. Duane Eddy's Rebel-'Rouser, The Ventures' Perfidia, Annette Funicello's Pineapple Princess, and Dick Dale and His Del-Tones' Misirlou give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.

mission_detail_history_module.compact: What this route tests: A California-coded early guitar-pop lane split between reverb-soaked instrumentals and harmony-rich beach-radio songs.
mission_detail_history_module.standard: Surf music turns place into sound: ocean motion, hot rods, Southern California youth imagery, and electric-guitar technology. Dick Dale and The Chantays show the instrumental attack; The Beach Boys and Jan and Dean show how surf culture became vocal pop mythology. It helps place this road in a broader music-history context.
